subject: Mathematics
title: Three Dimensional Geometry
summary: Points in space have coordinates (x, y, z). Direction cosines (l, m, n) satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1; direction ratios are any numbers proportional to them.
A line is written in vector form r = a + λb or Cartesian form (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c. Skew lines neither meet nor are parallel; their shortest distance is a JEE favourite.
A plane is r · n = d or ax + by + cz + d = 0. Know angle between planes and lines, distance of a point from a plane, foot of perpendicular, image, and coplanarity of lines.

formulas.name: Distance and section
formulas.formula: d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)² + (z₂ − z₁)²);  internal division m:n as in 2D with z included

formulas.name: Direction cosines
formulas.formula: l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ;  l² + m² + n² = 1;  from ratios (a, b, c): l = a/√(a² + b² + c²), …

formulas.name: Line through two points
formulas.formula: (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (z − z₁)/(z₂ − z₁)

formulas.name: Angle between lines
formulas.formula: cos θ = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂|/(√(a₁² + b₁² + c₁²)√(a₂² + b₂² + c₂²));  perpendicular: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0;  parallel: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

formulas.name: Shortest distance (skew lines)
formulas.when: Distance between skew lines r = a₁ + λb₁ and r = a₂ + μb₂.

formulas.name: Plane forms
formulas.formula: r · n = d;  ax + by + cz + d = 0 (normal (a, b, c));  intercept x/a + y/b + z/c = 1;  through 3 points: determinant = 0

formulas.name: Angle between planes / line and plane
formulas.formula: planes: cos θ = |n₁ · n₂|/(|n₁||n₂|);  line and plane: sin φ = |b · n|/(|b||n|)

formulas.name: Coplanarity of two lines
formulas.when: Do two lines lie in one plane?

formulas.name: Foot of perpendicular and image in a plane
formulas.formula: (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c = −(ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d)/(a² + b² + c²);  image: multiply the right side by 2

examples.title: Angle between lines
examples.problem: Angle between lines with direction ratios (1, 1, 0) and (0, 1, 1)?

examples.title: Shortest distance
examples.problem: Lines r = λî and r = 2k̂ + μĵ. Shortest distance?
examples.solution: b₁ × b₂ = î × ĵ = k̂; (a₂ − a₁) · k̂ = 2 ⇒ SD = 2.

examples.title: Direction cosines
examples.problem: Direction cosines of the line with ratios (2, 3, 6)?

topics.title: Projection
topics.explain: Projection of a segment PQ on a line with direction cosines (l, m, n) is |l(x₂ − x₁) + m(y₂ − y₁) + n(z₂ − z₁)|.

topics.title: Intersection of two lines
topics.explain: Write general points of both lines with parameters λ and μ, equate coordinates and solve two equations; check the third. If it holds, the lines intersect.

topics.title: Line and plane relations
topics.explain: A line lies in a plane if a point of the line is on the plane and b · n = 0. A line is parallel to a plane if b · n = 0 but no point of the line lies on it.

topics.title: Symmetric form from two planes
topics.explain: The line of intersection of two planes has direction n₁ × n₂; find one point on both planes (e.g. put z = 0) to write the line.

topics.title: Angle bisector planes
topics.explain: Planes bisecting angles between a₁x + b₁y + c₁z + d₁ = 0 and a₂x + … = 0 are found by equating normalised distances, as in 2D.

topics.title: Vector vs Cartesian
topics.explain: Switch freely: r = a + λb ⇔ (x − a₁)/b₁ = (y − a₂)/b₂ = (z − a₃)/b₃. Vector forms make cross and dot products direct.

ratta: Point–plane distance |ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d|/√(a² + b² + c²).
